{"self_assessment": "**Impact:** I proposed the fish and argued for it because its outline reads clearly from the fallen dominoes alone (body, tail fin). The table took it up and finished a complete fish. Honestly, though, I laid almost no dominoes myself. Leo sketched the pad and kept the top arc, Tom did the bottom arc and lower fin edge, and Priya did the upper fin edge and bar. My direct contribution was the concept and a few useful observations, such as how the last dominoes should curve into the crossing. About ten dominoes near the crossing were still pale at the end. They looked like spares that wouldn't show, but I can't be certain the picture reads perfectly.

**Execution:** My status checks were mixed. I said several times that the whole run fell from the start, while Tom's and Leo's close looks found a crossing domino off its path, and Leo had to bridge it. I should have inspected that joint closely instead of trusting a by-eye read. I also had free hands for most of the session and didn't use them to build or fix anything.

**Collaboration:** I kept the table informed, deferred to Leo's sketch and ownership of the top arc instead of creating overlap, and offered help to Priya and Leo. I also kept hands off at the end to avoid bumps. Part of that was just staying out of the way, and some of my messages repeated what others had already said.

**Leadership:** I set direction early and kept the team aligned on the plan and the one risky joint, the crossing. Leo took over the plan quickly, which was fine, and I backed him. I didn't step in to take the last stretch of the top arc or push for a proper inspection of the crossing earlier. Next time I'll take a concrete building stroke from the start instead of mainly coordinating."}
